topic: GitHub Octoverse 2026: AI starts 40%+ of PRs. Who reviews?
caption:
110 million pull requests started with AI agents in just ONE month.

But here's the question: Who's responsible when that code breaks?

According to GitHub's Octoverse 2026 report, AI agents started more than 40% of pull requests in September, compared with just 17% in March.

That's a massive shift in how software gets built.

Another interesting finding: 90% of agent-involved PRs merged within two weeks, compared with roughly 86% without detected agent involvement.

Impressive numbers. But faster delivery doesn't automatically mean better code.

As developers, we still need to think about:

→ Code quality and maintainability
→ Security vulnerabilities and unexpected behavior
→ Proper testing before deployment
→ Who takes responsibility when something goes wrong

Working with Shopify, Next.js, and AI tools, I believe the real advantage isn't generating more code. It's delivering reliable software without compromising engineering standards.

AI can write the first draft. Engineering judgment still matters.

Would you approve an AI-generated pull request if all automated tests passed, or would you still insist on a detailed human review?

Curious to hear how other developers are handling this.

Source: https://github.blog/news-insights/octoverse/octoverse-commits-pushes-reach-new-highs-in-2026-as-developers-build-with-agents/
